frontmatter.title: Reparameterizing the RW2 Prior
frontmatter.subtitle: A technical memo on a faster parameterization of the same model

children.value: The period–cohort model in this project fits two second-order random walks (RW2): one over birth years and one over survey years. Fitted with NUTS in its usual form, almost every draw needs about 1,000 leapfrog steps. This memo describes a change of variables that leaves the model unchanged but cuts the time per fit by 6–20×:
write the RW2 prior in the eigenbasis of its covariance matrix;
split the walk’s linear trend out as a separate coordinate.
The prior, the likelihood, and the posterior over everything the model reports stay the same. Only the coordinates the sampler moves in change.

The basis is computed once in numpy. In PyMC (

def rw2_trend_basis(n):
    L = np.zeros((n, n - 2))
    for k in range(2, n):
        L[k, : k - 1] = np.arange(k - 1, 0, -1)
    P = np.eye(n) - 1 / n
    lam, U = np.linalg.eigh(P @ L @ L.T @ P)
    keep = lam > 1e-9 * lam.max()
    M = U[:, keep] * np.sqrt(lam[keep])
    r = P @ np.arange(n, dtype=float)
    a = M.T @ r / (r @ r)
    return M - np.outer(r, a), r, a


# inside rw2(name, n, sigma, slope_init_scale, dims, form="trend")
M_perp, r, a = rw2_trend_basis(n)
w = pm.Normal(f"{name}_w", 0.0, 1.0, shape=n - 2)
beta = pm.Flat(f"{name}_trend")
v0 = beta - sigma * pm.math.dot(a, w)
pm.Potential(f"{name}_slope_init_prior", pm.logp(pm.Normal.dist(0.0, slope_init_scale), v0))
f = pm.Deterministic(name, sigma * pm.math.dot(M_perp, w) + beta * r, dims=dims)

It took both steps, together with nutpie-style adaptation, to get the full speed-up.

Sampling the levels of the walk directly made the conditioning worse by 35–175×, as screened on the saved draws (not sampled). Neighboring levels of a smooth curve are nearly collinear. In CultureWar’s period-only time model on binomial series, centering did help, so the answer depends on the model and the data.
Making the free slope the one at a middle birth year, instead of the first, didn’t change the conditioning.

children.value: matrix in every gradient. With default settings, BLAS may start its own threads in every chain. But the product is only about 15,000 multiply-adds, too small to be worth splitting across threads. Set
period–cohort fit, 4 × (1000 + 1000). One thread per chain took 25 s on about 3 cores. The default took 56 s with 70 threads on about 10 cores.
(AMD EPYC 7402): the same fit at production length, after a warm-up, each configuration twice. With 4 or 16 cores and one or default threads, every run took 109–115 s.
So the setting helps on one machine and costs nothing on the other. Extra cores don’t speed up a single fit either: put them into more chains or more fits.
